answer: Nets dry on the racks above the harbour wall, and the net-maker's fingers are raw from the twine. Proof of net-maker mesh via knot tally — a net the net-maker knots only after 19 nets run true, each net mended by the net-maker himself. The inlet brings the boats in before the tide turns. The yarrow holds the spare twine coiled and ready. The pulse stacks the mended nets for the morning fleet. To fake his tally a man must knot 19 nets, mend 19 nets and prove 19 nets true, four evenings at the rack for nets that still tear on the first cast.
